symptom: Any Google call fails with "403 unauthorized_client" or "Client is unauthorized to retrieve access tokens using this method".
likely_cause: The service account's Client ID is not listed under domain-wide delegation, or it was listed with a different scope set than the code now asks for.
steps: Ask Trevor for the service-account Client ID (a long number). He can print it with: gcloud iam service-accounts describe ntxp-workspace-agent@ntxp-workspace-agent.iam.gserviceaccount.com --format='value(oauth2ClientId)'.
Sign in to https://admin.google.com/ac/owl/domainwidedelegation as a Workspace super admin.
Find the row with that Client ID. If there is none, click Add new.
Get the full scope list by running: python3 scripts/google_workspace/ntxp_google_access.py scopes --csv. Paste it into the OAuth scopes box exactly, replacing what is there, and click Authorize.
Wait 5 minutes (Google can take up to 24 hours, usually minutes), then test with: python3 scripts/google_workspace/ntxp_google_access.py whoami.
If it still fails after one hour, escalate.

symptom: One Google area works (for example Gmail) but another fails with "access_denied" or "Requested scope not authorized" (often Admin Reports, Contacts or Calendar).
likely_cause: A scope was added to the access layer after delegation was set up, so the delegation entry is missing it.
steps: Run: python3 scripts/google_workspace/ntxp_google_access.py scopes --csv and copy the output.
Open https://admin.google.com/ac/owl/domainwidedelegation, click the NTXP Workspace Agent row, then Edit.
Compare the scope list. Replace it with the full copied list (do not remove scopes that are still in the copied list).
Save, wait 5 minutes, retry the failing screen in the admin console.
Write the date and the scope you added into this entry's notes in the Admin Runbook sheet.

symptom: setup_dwd.sh prints "Key creation blocked by org policy; using keyless mode instead", or Cloud Console says service account key creation is disabled.
likely_cause: The Google Cloud org policy iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation is on. Keyless mode works on a laptop but the VPS container has no Google login, so the admin console needs a key.
steps: Do not try to switch the policy off for the whole organization.
Escalate to Trevor with the exact message. He decides between (a) a policy exception for the single project ntxp-workspace-agent only, or (b) keyless mode with a workload identity on the VPS.

If an exception is approved: in Cloud Console go to IAM & Admin > Organization Policies, select project ntxp-workspace-agent, open 'Disable service account key creation', choose Override parent's policy, set Enforcement Off, save.
Re-run: bash scripts/google_workspace/setup_dwd.sh. Move the key contents into the NTXP vault as NTXP_GOOGLE_SA_KEY and delete the local file in ~/.config/ntxp/.
Re-enable the policy override (Enforcement On) once the key is created.

symptom: Error says the user to impersonate is outside the domain, or "subject must be an @ntxpllc.com user".
likely_cause: Someone asked the tool to act as a personal Gmail, a contractor address, or a misspelled address. The access layer refuses anything outside ntxpllc.com by design.
steps: Check the address for typos (for example ntxpllc.co or ntxp.com).
Use the person's @ntxpllc.com address. External people cannot be impersonated; ask them to share the file or message instead.
Do not change NTXP_GOOGLE_DOMAIN to get around this.

symptom: "invalid_grant" or "Invalid email or User ID" when reading one person's mailbox or Drive.
likely_cause: That account is suspended, deleted, renamed, or has no Gmail/Drive licence.
steps: Open https://admin.google.com > Directory > Users and search the name.
If suspended or deleted, this is expected; the analytics skip that person. Note it on the flag and dismiss.
If renamed, use the new primary address (aliases cannot be impersonated).
If the account has no licence, Trevor decides whether to assign one.

symptom: Server log shows a JSON decode error or "Could not deserialize key data" on start-up; every Google source shows error.
likely_cause: NTXP_GOOGLE_SA_KEY was pasted with broken line breaks, extra quotes, or only part of the JSON.
steps: Open the NTXP vault entry for NTXP_GOOGLE_SA_KEY and confirm it starts with { and ends with } and contains "private_key".
In Hostinger hPanel > VPS > Docker Manager > ntxp-admin project > Environment, paste the value again as one line (the \n sequences inside private_key must stay as the two characters backslash and n).
Restart the project (Docker Manager > Restart) and check /api/health from the console's Status card.
Never paste the key into chat, email, a ticket or this runbook.

symptom: The console Status card shows gmail, drive, calendar, contacts, directory and reports as "unconfigured".
likely_cause: The VPS project environment is missing NTXP_GOOGLE_SA_KEY (or NTXP_GOOGLE_SA_EMAIL) or NTXP_GOOGLE_ADMIN_SUBJECT, or NTXP_ADMIN_DEMO is still on.
steps: In hPanel open the VPS > Docker Manager > ntxp-admin > Environment.
Confirm NTXP_GOOGLE_SA_KEY and NTXP_GOOGLE_ADMIN_SUBJECT are present and not empty. Copy missing values from the NTXP vault.
Confirm NTXP_ADMIN_DEMO is empty or false in production.
Restart the project and reload the Status card.

symptom: User list or login reports fail with "Not Authorized to access this resource/api" while Gmail and Drive work.
likely_cause: NTXP_GOOGLE_ADMIN_SUBJECT is a normal user, not a Workspace super admin; the Admin Directory and Reports APIs need an admin to impersonate.
steps: In https://admin.google.com > Account > Admin roles, check that the account in NTXP_GOOGLE_ADMIN_SUBJECT holds Super Admin.
If not, set NTXP_GOOGLE_ADMIN_SUBJECT to an account that does (ask Trevor which).
Granting a new super admin is an owner decision; do not grant it yourself.

symptom: A Google service-account key, OAuth client secret or API key was pasted somewhere public (GitHub, email, chat, a shared doc).
likely_cause: Human or agent error. The repo is public; anything committed is exposed immediately.
steps: Treat it as an incident now, not later. Tell Trevor and Alison by phone.
Trevor: delete the exposed key in Cloud Console > IAM & Admin > Service Accounts > ntxp-workspace-agent > Keys.
Trevor: if a service-account key leaked, remove the Client ID at https://admin.google.com/ac/owl/domainwidedelegation until a new key is issued.
Create a new key, store it only in the NTXP vault and the VPS project environment, restart the project.
Remove the secret from the place it leaked (a git history rewrite needs Trevor). Log what happened in the Learning tab.

symptom: After choosing a Google account, admin.ntxpllc.com shows the oauth2-proxy "403 Forbidden / Permission Denied" page for Trevor or Alison.
likely_cause: The browser signed in with a different Google account (personal Gmail or an alias), or the address is missing or misspelled in admin_console/deploy/emails.txt (and the inline copy in docker-compose.yaml).
steps: Open https://admin.ntxpllc.com/oauth2/sign_out, then sign in again and pick exactly trevor@ntxpllc.com or alison@ntxpllc.com.
Try a private/incognito window to rule out a second signed-in Google account.
If it still fails, Trevor checks emails.txt and the emails config block in docker-compose.yaml: each address on its own line, lower case, no spaces.
Editing the allowed list is a permission change (Tier 3) and needs owner approval before redeploy.

symptom: Google shows "Error 400: redirect_uri_mismatch" when signing in.
likely_cause: The OAuth web client in Google Cloud does not list https://admin.ntxpllc.com/oauth2/callback exactly, or OAUTH2_PROXY_CLIENT_ID points at a different client.
steps: In Google Cloud Console > APIs & Services > Credentials, open the 'NTXP Admin Console' OAuth client.
Under Authorized redirect URIs make sure this exact line exists: https://admin.ntxpllc.com/oauth2/callback (https, no trailing slash).
Confirm the Client ID shown there matches OAUTH2_PROXY_CLIENT_ID in the VPS project environment.
Save, wait 5 minutes, try again.

symptom: The page keeps bouncing between Google and admin.ntxpllc.com (sign-in loop), or says "cookie not found" / CSRF error.
likely_cause: The cookie secret changed or is the wrong length, the site was opened over http, or the browser blocks cookies for the site.
steps: Clear cookies for admin.ntxpllc.com (browser settings > Privacy > Site data), close the tab, open https://admin.ntxpllc.com again.
Make sure the address starts with https://. The proxy only sets secure cookies.
Trevor: confirm OAUTH2_PROXY_COOKIE_SECRET is exactly 32 characters (generated as in DEPLOY.md step b). If it was regenerated, everyone must sign in again; that is expected.
Trevor: confirm the VPS clock is correct (timedatectl). A clock off by minutes breaks Google tokens.

symptom: Google sign-in succeeds but the console shows {"code": "not_owner"} or a blank panel with 403 on every /api call.
likely_cause: The app is not receiving the X-Forwarded-Email header: oauth2-proxy is missing --pass-user-headers, or someone reached the app container directly.
steps: Trevor: check the oauth2-proxy command in docker-compose.yaml includes --pass-user-headers=true and --upstream=http://app:8080.
Confirm the app service has no ports: section (it must only be reachable through oauth2-proxy).
Redeploy and retry. Do not weaken the server's owner check to make it work.

symptom: An NTXP employee (not Trevor or Alison) reports they get 403 at admin.ntxpllc.com.
likely_cause: Working as designed. Only the two owners may use the console.
steps: Tell the employee the console is owner-only and no action is needed.
Do not add them to emails.txt. Access for anyone else is an owner decision.
If the employee needs data from the console, ask Trevor to share the specific report.

symptom: After signing in, the page shows "502 Bad Gateway" or "upstream connect error".
likely_cause: oauth2-proxy is up but the app container is stopped, crashing or still starting.
steps: Wait 60 seconds and reload; the app may be restarting.
If it persists, follow RB-016 (container down).

symptom: admin.ntxpllc.com does not load, shows 502, or Docker Manager shows a container as Exited/Restarting.
likely_cause: The app or proxy container crashed (bad env value, code error after a deploy) or the VPS rebooted.
steps: In hPanel > VPS > Docker Manager, open the ntxp-admin project and note which container is not Running.
Open its Logs and copy the last 30 lines into the ticket (remove anything that looks like a key).
Click Restart on the project (API: VPS_restartProjectV1). Restart keeps data.
If it crashes again with the same log, stop and escalate with the log lines.
Do not click Delete on the project.

symptom: App container logs show ModuleNotFoundError, ImportError or "Error loading ASGI app" right after a deploy.
likely_cause: The new code has a missing dependency or a file path changed; the image built from an older or partial commit.
steps: Trevor: check the commit on the default branch builds locally: docker build -f admin_console/deploy/Dockerfile .
Add the missing package to admin_console/server/requirements.txt, push, then redeploy (DEPLOY.md step d).
To get back up fast, roll back per DEPLOY.md step g.

symptom: Browser warns "Your connection is not private" or Caddy logs show "obtaining certificate" errors / ACME challenge failed.
likely_cause: DNS for admin.ntxpllc.com does not point at the VPS yet, ports 80/443 are blocked by the VPS firewall, or another proxy already holds 80/443.
steps: Check DNS first (RB-019). Caddy cannot get a certificate until admin.ntxpllc.com resolves to the VPS IP.
In hPanel > VPS > Firewall, confirm inbound TCP 80 and 443 are allowed.
If the VPS already runs a reverse proxy (the MCP gateway's), do not use the tls profile; route admin.ntxpllc.com through that proxy instead (DEPLOY.md step d).
After fixing, restart the project and wait 2 minutes for the certificate.

symptom: admin.ntxpllc.com "site can't be reached" / DNS_PROBE_FINISHED_NXDOMAIN, or it resolves to the wrong IP.
likely_cause: The A record was not created, was created on the wrong name, or has not propagated yet.
steps: Check at https://dns.google/query?name=admin.ntxpllc.com&type=A. The answer must be the VPS IP from hPanel.
If there is no answer, ask Trevor to run the DNS chain in DEPLOY.md step e (snapshot, validate, update with overwrite false, verify).
If the answer is right but your computer still fails, wait up to the record's TTL (default 300 s to 1 hour) or try on phone data.
DNS changes on ntxpllc.com are Tier 3 and need owner approval; never change MX, NS or other records while fixing this.

symptom: A Hostinger API or MCP call fails: 401, 405, timeout, "Server already initialized", or the connector will not start.
likely_cause: Known Hostinger gateway defects or an API outage. Two failures on the same tier mean descend the ladder.
steps: Read the Hostinger run journal (hostinger-run-journal.json in Drive) for a known defect and the tier to start at.
Tier 1 MCP gateway failed twice: Tier 2, direct REST to developers.hostinger.com with the vault token.
Tier 2 failed: Tier 3, do the step by hand in hPanel (https://hpanel.hostinger.com) in Trevor's logged-in browser.
Tier 3 unavailable: Tier 4 LMCP saved browser session; then Tier 5 SSH/curl to the VPS from the Mac.
Append what worked to the run journal so the next attempt starts there.

symptom: Project fails to start with "port is already allocated" or "bind: address already in use" for 80, 443 or 4180.
likely_cause: Another project on the VPS (usually the MCP gateway's reverse proxy) already uses that port.
steps: Remove COMPOSE_PROFILES=tls from the project environment so Caddy does not start.
If 4180 clashes, set OAUTH2_PROXY_BIND_PORT to a free port such as 4181 in the project environment.
Add a site for admin.ntxpllc.com to the existing proxy pointing at 127.0.0.1:<that port> (DEPLOY.md step d, option 1).
Restart the project.

symptom: A fix was merged on GitHub but the live console still behaves the old way.
likely_cause: Update/restart reuses the already-built image; the app image is only rebuilt when the project is re-created.
steps: Trevor: re-run VPS_createNewProjectV1 with the same project name and the GitHub repo URL (DEPLOY.md step d) so Docker rebuilds from the latest commit.
Hard-refresh the browser (Ctrl+Shift+R) to drop cached web files.
Confirm the change, then log the deploy in the run journal.

symptom: The Hostinger connector stops responding in the middle of a deploy or restart.
likely_cause: The MCP gateway runs on the same VPS. Restarting shared proxy or Docker services drops the connector mid-call.
steps: Wait 2 minutes, then retry the read call (VPS_getProjectListV1).
If it stays down, continue in hPanel by hand (tier ladder step 3).
Before future restarts, warn that the connector will drop.

symptom: After a DNS change, company email, the website or mcp.ntxpllc.cloud stopped working.
likely_cause: A DNS update overwrote or removed records it should not have (usually overwrite set to true).
steps: Call Trevor immediately; mail outages are silent.
Trevor: list snapshots (DNS_getDNSSnapshotListV1 for ntxpllc.com), inspect the one taken before the change (DNS_getDNSSnapshotV1), then restore it (DNS_restoreDNSSnapshotV1).
Verify MX and the website resolve again, then redo only the admin A record with overwrite false.
Tell Alison what broke and for how long.

symptom: Contacts labelled for sharing never show up in the Shared Contacts list.
likely_cause: The Google Contacts label is not spelled exactly "★ NTXP Shared" (star, space, NTXP, space, Shared), or the label does not exist in that user's Contacts.
steps: Open https://contacts.google.com as that user and look at the labels in the left menu.
If missing, create a label and copy-paste the name from this entry: ★ NTXP Shared.
If a similar label exists (no star, extra space), rename it to the exact name.
In the console, open Shared Contacts and click Sync now (POST /api/contacts/sync).

symptom: The same person appears two or more times in Shared Contacts after an import or sync.
likely_cause: The duplicate records have different emails or phone formats, so the de-duplication did not match them; or an import was committed without reviewing the duplicates list.
steps: Always import with Preview first (commit=false) and read the Duplicates list before committing.
For existing duplicates: open each, copy any missing phone/email into the best record with Edit.
Select the extra records and choose Delete. Delete is Tier 3: the console shows a summary and waits for an owner to approve.
Approve within 15 minutes or the request expires and must be restaged.

symptom: Import says the file format was not detected, or the preview shows names in the wrong columns.
likely_cause: The file is not one of the supported layouts (vCard .vcf, Google CSV, Outlook CSV, simple CSV with a header row) or it was saved in a non-UTF-8 encoding.
steps: Re-export from the source: Google Contacts > Export > Google CSV, or Outlook > Export > CSV, or the phone's .vcf.
If it is a spreadsheet, save as CSV UTF-8 with a header row (Name, Email, Phone, Company, Title).
In the import dialog, pick the format by hand instead of Auto.
Preview again before committing.

symptom: Sync reports errors for one user, or a user's personal contacts never appear.
likely_cause: The contacts scope is missing from domain-wide delegation, or the user's account is suspended.
steps: Check the Status card: contacts must be "ok".
If it says error, follow RB-002 to add the contacts scopes.
If only one user fails, check the account in Admin console (RB-005).

symptom: A bulk action (delete, unshare many) shows "needs approval" and nothing happens.
likely_cause: Working as designed: deletes and bulk actions are Tier 3 and wait for an owner's approval.
steps: Read the summary. It names how many contacts and which action.
If correct, an owner clicks Approve on the same screen. Approval is bound to that exact list.
If the list changes, the approval is void; stage it again.
Staged changes expire after 15 minutes.

symptom: A person shows no data (blank row or zero activity) on the analytics page.
likely_cause: The person's account is new, suspended or unlicensed; they are not assigned to any project in NTXP_PROJECT_ASSIGNMENTS; or the Google sources are unconfigured.
steps: Check the Status card. If gmail/directory are not "ok", fix that first (RB-007).
Confirm the person's account is active in Admin console > Directory > Users.
Ask Trevor whether the person is listed in NTXP_PROJECT_ASSIGNMENTS for their jobs.
Click Run analysis now and wait for the next cycle.
No data is never a reason to flag the person.

symptom: A flag looks wrong (for example "slow responses" while the person was on vacation, at a job site, or out sick).
likely_cause: The cross-check did not find the explanation: no calendar out-of-office, no JobTread time entry, or the reason was discussed by phone.
steps: Open the flag and read Cross-check: which sources were checked and what was found.
If you know the reason, choose Dismiss and write the reason in the note (for example: PTO 10/6-10/8 approved by Trevor).
Ask the person to use Google Calendar out-of-office for future absences so the system explains them automatically.
Flags are proposals for the owners. No flag is ever used for discipline without owner review.

symptom: A level 2 escalation shows as sent but the owner never received the email.
likely_cause: NTXP_ALERT_SENDER is empty or not a real mailbox, the gmail.send scope is missing, or the message went to spam.
steps: Search the owner's Spam and All Mail for "NTXP Alert".
Check that NTXP_ALERT_SENDER is an active @ntxpllc.com mailbox (for example alerts@ntxpllc.com).
Check the delegation scopes include gmail.send (RB-002).
Mark a found message as Not spam so future alerts land in the inbox.

symptom: A level 3 SMS escalation failed or never arrived; Status shows quo as error or unconfigured.
likely_cause: QUO_API_KEY is missing or revoked, QUO_FROM_NUMBER is not a Quo number on the account, or NTXP_ALISON_SMS / NTXP_TREVOR_SMS is not in +1XXXXXXXXXX form.
steps: Check the Status card for quo.
Confirm the phone variables look like +12145550123 (plus sign, country code, no spaces or dashes).
In the Quo app, confirm QUO_FROM_NUMBER is one of the company's inboxes and the API key is active.
Until fixed, call the owner directly for any level 3 item.

symptom: A level 3 item happened overnight but the SMS arrived only in the morning.
likely_cause: Quiet hours (9 pm to 6 am Central). Non-critical texts are held until 6 am; only critical urgency goes out overnight.
steps: This is expected behaviour. Check the flag's urgency: only "critical" overrides quiet hours.
If an owner wants a category treated as critical, that is an owner decision; record it and tell Trevor.
Do not change the quiet-hours setting yourself.

symptom: An emotional-volatility score appears for a customer, vendor or other non-NTXP person, or appears anywhere outside the owner console.
likely_cause: Defect. Volatility is computed only for NTXP-to-NTXP internal messages and is internal-only.
steps: Stop sharing or exporting that report.
Screenshot the screen (crop out message text) and send it to Trevor.
Trevor disables analytics runs until fixed and deletes the stray value.
Tell Alison if the value left the console.

symptom: Dashboard tiles never update until the page is reloaded.
likely_cause: The live update stream (/api/analytics/stream) is being buffered by a proxy in front of oauth2-proxy.
steps: Reload the page; numbers will be current at load.
Trevor: if an existing proxy fronts the console, turn off response buffering for admin.ntxpllc.com (nginx: proxy_buffering off; Caddy: flush_interval -1).
Confirm the tiles move during the next Run analysis now.

symptom: The console shows sample names or a "Demo" badge in production.
likely_cause: NTXP_ADMIN_DEMO is set to true in the VPS project environment.
steps: In hPanel > Docker Manager > ntxp-admin > Environment, clear NTXP_ADMIN_DEMO (or set it to false).
Restart the project.
Never act on, export or forward demo numbers.

symptom: An employee asks whether they are being monitored, objects to monitoring, or files a complaint about a flag.
likely_cause: Normal question; the monitoring notice may not have reached them or they want to talk about a specific decision.
steps: Do not discuss flags, scores or another person's data with the employee.
Give them a copy of the signed Employee Monitoring Notice (docs/EMPLOYEE_MONITORING_NOTICE.md) if they have not received one.
Pass the question to Alison the same day. Legal or HR responses come from the owner, with counsel if needed.

symptom: NTXP Form Fill finds no fields (or too few) in a blank form.
likely_cause: The PDF is a scan or flattened print with no fillable (AcroForm) fields, so only visual detection can find blanks.
steps: Run: python scripts/nff_detect_fields.py --form <file>.pdf --output-json fields.json and check the count.
If 0 AcroForm fields, ask the sender for a fillable PDF; agencies often have one on their website.
Otherwise let NTXP Form Fill use overlay mode and review every field in the approval GUI (expect more red Manual fields).
Log the form name in the Learning tab as gap_found so it becomes a prewired workflow.

symptom: The filled PDF opens with empty boxes even though the approval screen showed values.
likely_cause: The viewer is not regenerating field appearances (common in Preview on Mac or browser viewers), or the form uses XFA.
steps: Open the file in Adobe Acrobat Reader; values usually appear there.
If still empty, re-run nff_fill_pdf.py with overlay mode so values are drawn on the page.
If the form is XFA (Acrobat says 'Please wait...' or 'dynamic form'), request a standard PDF from the agency or print to PDF first.

symptom: Signature step stops with "needs_circumstance" or "signer not allowed".
likely_cause: Trevor was named as signer without a stated circumstance, or a name other than Alison Hopkins or Trevor Hopkins was entered.
steps: Default: change the signer to Alison Hopkins (designated signatory).
If Alison truly cannot sign (for example travelling and the deadline is today), Trevor may sign: type the circumstance in plain words so it is recorded.
No one else can sign for NTXP. Do not type another name.

symptom: A signature that was approved is now refused with "approval void" or digest mismatch.
likely_cause: A field or the file changed after approval. Approval is bound to the exact file (hash), signer and fields.
steps: This is a safety feature. Review the changed form again in the approval GUI.
Request a new approval for the new version.
Do not edit the form after approval; make all edits first, then approve.

symptom: A form came out with an old address (405 S Elm St Ste 203), an old phone, or the wrong owner/contact name.
likely_cause: A Drive scan or old KB row offered a retired value. Tier 1 identity rules always win: Owner Alison Hopkins, Operations contact Trevor Hopkins, 101 South Locust St Ste 605, Denton, TX 76201, phone 469-248-7431.
steps: Do not send the form. Correct the field in the approval GUI to the Tier 1 value.
In the NTXP Form Fill KB sheet, mark the old value as retired: in the alternates column so it is blocked in future.
If an agency's own records show the retired value and they require a change form, that is an owner decision.
Log the correction in the Learning tab.

symptom: A W-9 shows the LLC box checked or a letter in the LLC tax-classification code.
likely_cause: The form was filled outside the W-9 workflow or a manual edit overrode it.
steps: Line 3a must have only S corporation checked. Uncheck LLC and clear the LLC code box.
Re-run the fill through the W-9 prewired workflow, which fixes these values.
Get a fresh signature approval (RB-042) before the W-9 leaves NTXP.

symptom: Work is paused with a Council "gate" message showing options A/B/C.
likely_cause: The Council needs a human decision: a methodology, classification, privacy or payment choice, or spend hit 75% of a ceiling.
steps: Read the gate text; it includes a recommendation.
Methodology, classification or tool choices: Trevor decides. Payment or anything money-related: Alison decides.
Reply with the chosen option. Agents never pick an option for the owners.
Open gates are also emailed and texted automatically within a minute.

symptom: Council or analytics refuse to run: "cost ceiling reached" ($2 per task, $15 per day, $150 per month).
likely_cause: Spend hit a ceiling. The live values are in the Council sheet's 01 Config tab.
steps: Wait for the daily reset (midnight Central) for the day ceiling.
Deterministic (Tier 0) analytics keep running; only model steps pause.
Raising a ceiling spends money and is Alison's decision. Send her the gate text and the cost summary.

symptom: A Council provider is down (errors or timeouts from one seat) or fewer than 3 providers are available.
likely_cause: Provider outage, expired API key (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, XAI_API_KEY or others in the vault), or NTXP_COUNCIL_URL unreachable.
steps: Check the provider's status page and the Council sheet's 31 Environments tab.
Retry once after 10 minutes.
If the key is expired, Trevor rotates it in the vault and the VPS environment.
Councils need at least 3 distinct providers. If fewer are up, wait; do not replace them with DeepSeek or GLM for personnel or owner content.

symptom: Status shows jobtread as error, or JobTread-based tiles (daily reports, PO/invoice integrity) are empty.
likely_cause: JOBTREAD_GRANT_KEY is missing, expired or was revoked in JobTread.
steps: In JobTread, Settings > API, check that the NTXP Admin Console grant is still active.
If not, Trevor creates a new grant key, saves it in the vault, and updates JOBTREAD_GRANT_KEY in the VPS environment.
Restart the project and click Run analysis now.

symptom: JobTread data shows up, but people are matched to the wrong jobs or a project is missing from reports.
likely_cause: NTXP_PROJECT_ASSIGNMENTS does not list the job or the person, or the JobTread job name changed.
steps: Ask Trevor for the current project assignment list (job name and the people on it).
Trevor updates NTXP_PROJECT_ASSIGNMENTS in the VPS environment (each person's email with their projects and Drive folder IDs); project names must match JobTread exactly.
Restart and rerun the analysis. Dismiss flags caused by the wrong assignment with a note.

symptom: Plaud recordings or transcripts are missing; Status shows plaud as error or unconfigured.
likely_cause: PLAUD_API_KEY is missing or expired, or the recording was never synced from the device to the Plaud cloud.
steps: On the Plaud app, confirm the recording shows as synced and transcribed.
If it is synced but missing in the console, Trevor checks PLAUD_API_KEY in the vault and VPS environment.
Recordings are confidential personnel content; never forward transcripts outside the owners.

symptom: git push from a Claude Code cloud session fails with 403 from the proxy or "permission denied".
likely_cause: The session's GitHub access is read-only for that repository, or the GitHub App is not installed for the account.
steps: In the session, ask Claude to run check_repo_access for the repository and read the push verdict.
If refused, Trevor reconnects GitHub at claude.ai > Settings > Connectors or installs the Claude GitHub App on the repo.
Retry the push once access shows ok. Retrying before that does not help.

symptom: Push rejected: "non-fast-forward", "fetch first" or "protected branch".
likely_cause: Someone pushed to the branch since the session started, or the session tried to push directly to the default branch.
steps: Ask Claude to push to a new feature branch and open a pull request instead of pushing to master/main.
For non-fast-forward on a feature branch: fetch, rebase on the remote branch, rerun tests, push again.
Never force-push to the default branch.

symptom: Push blocked by GitHub secret scanning ("push protection: secret detected").
likely_cause: A key or token was committed. The repository is public.
steps: Do not bypass the block.
Remove the secret from the commit (amend or rewrite the unpushed commits) and push again.
Treat the secret as exposed anyway and rotate it (RB-009).
Keys belong only in the NTXP vault and VPS environment variables.

symptom: Push or clone stalls, then fails with "RPC failed", "connection reset" or "unexpected disconnect".
likely_cause: The cloud session's outbound proxy cut off a large transfer.
steps: Retry once.
Ask Claude to check the agent proxy status page described in /root/.ccr/README.md and apply the fix it lists.
Avoid committing large binaries (images, PDFs); the .gitignore already excludes most.
